item.title: Jilin University lab leverages AI to study ancient Chinese scripts and relics
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
A member of the Key Laboratory of Ancient Chinese Script, Culture Relics and Artificial Intelligence of Jilin University observes details of pottery inscriptions of the Warring States Period (475 BC-221 BC) at Jilin University in Changchun, northeast China's Jilin Province, Sept. 2, 2026. Established in 2023, the Key Laboratory of Ancient Chinese Script, Culture Relics and Artificial Intelligence of Jilin University brings together researchers in the fields of paleography, archaeology, history, artificial intelligence, etc. With oracle bone inscriptions, bronze inscriptions, Warring States scripts, and Qin and Han scripts as core subjects for research, the laboratory sorts and catalogs scripts and culture relics in a systematic manner, and facilitates its work with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. "We hope to bridge the past and the present via AI, and accelerate research of ancient characters with a 'smart engine,' and 'wake up' the ancient books and documents that have been dormant for ages," said Li Chuntao, director of the laboratory. item.title: China's AI advances, inclusive governance approach gain global significance, says Polish scholar
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
The significance of China's experience extends beyond its technological progress. China has brought greater attention to capacity-building and the participation of developing countries in global discussions on AI governance, a Polish AI scholar has said. KARPACZ, Poland, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China has made substantial progress in artificial intelligence (AI), and its development-oriented and inclusive approach to AI governance is also gaining global significance, a Polish AI scholar has said. "China has done something quite unusual in AI in less than a decade," Lukasz Gacek, head of the Department of China at the Institute of the Middle and Far East at Jagiellonian University, told Xinhua in a recent interview on the sidelines of the 35th Economic Forum in Karpacz, southwestern Poland. Gacek has been an expert on contemporary China, global governance, energy transition and AI in international politics. Gacek closely followed the rollout of China's New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan in 2017, when he was working in Shanghai. The strategy set out a three-stage roadmap: keeping pace with leading countries in AI technology and applications by 2020, achieving major theoretical breakthroughs by 2025, and becoming a major global center for AI innovation by 2030. "What caught my attention was how quickly the plan moved beyond government institutions and entered universities, companies and other fields," Gacek said. One example, Gacek said, is the rapid expansion of AI education since 2017. Around that time, Chinese universities were beginning to establish dedicated AI degree programs. Less than a decade later, his research shows that more than 300 Chinese universities offer dedicated AI degree programs, while hundreds of others have introduced AI-related courses or integrated AI into their broader curricula. In his view, the significance of China's experience extends beyond its technological progress. China has brought greater attention to capacity-building and the participation of developing countries in global discussions on AI governance. Much of the international discussion on AI has focused on safety, regulation and competition among leading technological powers. China, Gacek said, has raised an important question: How can countries without advanced chips, large AI models or sufficient computing infrastructure participate meaningfully in the AI transformation? In July 2024, the UN General Assembly adopted a China-led resolution on strengthening international cooperation on AI capacity-building. Later that year, China put forward an action plan for inclusive AI development, with proposals covering infrastructure, open-source cooperation, training and exchanges on AI governance. Gacek added that similar priorities can be seen in China's cooperation with African countries, ASEAN members and BRICS countries. This has particular appeal for developing countries, as it promises to help them build their own technological capacity and gain a stronger voice in shaping the rules governing emerging technologies, Gacek said. ■

item.title: Roundup: Houthis seize Yemen's entire western coast after taking Bab al-Mandab Strait area
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
ADEN, Yemen, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Yemen's Houthi group seized Yemen's entire western coast and pushed its offensive beyond the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait into the southern province of Lahj on Friday, firing ballistic missiles at retreating government forces, government and military officials said. Earlier Friday, Houthi forces raided Mayun Island, also known as Perim Island, which lies at the heart of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and divides the narrow waterway into two shipping channels, after government troops withdrew overnight, a government official told Xinhua. "Houthi naval forces aboard several boats reached Mayun early Friday. They landed on the island and took control without military resistance," the official said, noting that the Houthis now hold "full grip over the Bab al-Mandab area." The advance followed the Houthis' Thursday capture of Mocha, a strategic Red Sea port city in southwestern Yemen. "After tightening their grip on Bab al-Mandab and key coastal areas and islands in and around the strait, the Houthis are pressing farther south," a Yemeni military official said Friday on condition of anonymity. Government forces have pulled back to Khor Omeira in Lahj, about 90 km west of Aden, the temporary seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government in the southern coast, the official said, adding that the forces "are regrouping with no clear indication of their next move." Residents in Khor Omeira reported signs of disarray among the retreating government forces, with some soldiers said to be selling their weapons at low prices and others discarding their uniforms before heading toward Aden. As the front line shifted closer to Aden, security forces reinforced the city's western approaches, according to a local security official. In a statement broadcast by Houthi-run al-Masirah TV on Friday, the Houthi spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the group's offensive, launched on Sept. 3, had seized about 5,400 square km of territory in western Yemen. He also claimed Houthi forces confronted Saudi warplanes in 32 engagements and "shot down nine aircraft." The claims could not be independently verified. Addressing concerns over the security of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Sarea said international maritime traffic remained "safe," while reiterating that Saudi vessels remained subject to Houthi restrictions. The Houthis announced a ban on Saudi shipping on July 20 and have since claimed a series of attacks on Saudi tankers and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia. Bab al-Mandab, which connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean, is a major route for international trade and energy shipments. Yemen has been embroiled in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of the country's north. The rapid Houthi advance marked the sharpest escalation since a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major hostilities. ■

item.title: Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
MasterOfCrafts | Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story -Xinhua MasterOfCrafts | Whispers of Chinese characters on ceramic glaze: A ceramic micro-calligraphy inheritor's story Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-11 21:32:16 JINGDEZHEN, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- There goes an old Chinese saying that "the scenery changes with each step." This saying can be true when you look at a ceramic micro-calligraphy artwork, on which Chinese characters are written in tiny little sizes so that you can not even notice them from a distance. Micro-calligraphy, or weishu, is an age-old Chinese art that wields the traditional Chinese writing brush to produce Chinese characters of astonishing minuteness with naked vision. This art form has deep roots in antiquity, with its earliest traces found in the oracle bone inscriptions from the Western Zhou Dynasty (1046 BC-771 BC). Ceramic micro-calligraphy, which combines the delicate art with polychrome ceramic, demands high in its making as the ceramic needs to go through high-temperature firing in kiln after the writing. To create a piece, the craftsman, relying solely on his naked eyes, uses a custom fashioned brush, with ultra-fine hairs and high-temperature-resistant pigments, to paint delicate motifs directly onto the ceramic's surface, no errors or corrections allowed. When the ceramic goes through repeated firings in the kiln, even the slightest deviation in temperature control can make all previous labors in vain. Upon completion, the artwork is seen with tiny little Chinese characters interlaced with paintings, complementing each other beautifully. The art has become a treasure of traditional Chinese crafts with irreplaceable artistic values, and was inscribed as one of China's national-level intangible cultural heritages in 2014. Liu Dachuan, a 47-year-old senior craftsman from south China's Guangdong Province, has dedicated himself to the art of ceramic micro-calligraphy for decades. He can inscribe up to 163 Chinese characters on a single square centimeter of porcelain, all perfectly distinguishable under a magnifying glass. Liu has formed a modern artistic style while carrying on the traditions, and his works have won multiple widely recognized awards. "Writing micro-calligraphy with the naked eye tests not only your eyesight, but also your very soul," Liu said, adding that a machine might replicate the shapes of characters, but it could never depict the flowing spirit unique to the tip of a brush. To bring ceramic micro-calligraphy to a wider audience, Liu held solo thematic exhibitions, and further established a studio in Jingdezhen, where he formally accepts apprentices and guides them step by step in the art. He also hosts public welfare open classes and intangible cultural heritage experiencing salons, where he offers lectures on the history of micro-calligraphy to local ceramics artisans and tourists on study tours. Regarded as premium collectible art pieces, ceramic micro-calligraphy artworks have won great favor from cultural institutions and museums, collectors and art lovers across the country. Meanwhile, as craftworks embodying the charm of oriental beauty, they have also appeared in exhibitions of many foreign countries, often being selected as gifts for culture exchanges, and being collected by overseas museums. In a way, they have become artistic carriers to promote the traditional Chinese culture and the exchanges between China and the world.

item.title: China slams U.S. espionage against Chinese enterprises
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Friday voiced "grave concerns" and "firm opposition" over a U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) official's remarks on taking Chinese enterprises as allegedly legitimate targets for espionage, urging an immediate cessation of such activities. "The U.S. side's brazen claims that Chinese enterprises are legitimate targets for espionage have thoroughly ripped off the fig leaf behind which intelligence agencies covertly steal secrets, exposing the bandit logic of hegemony in broad daylight," a ministry spokesperson said. China solemnly urges the U.S. side to immediately cease all espionage activities against China, including against Chinese enterprises, and to stop all actions that undermine China's sovereignty, security and development interests, said the spokesperson. China possesses "the firm will and ample means" to resolutely take necessary measures in accordance with laws and regulations, such as the Counter-Espionage Law, to severely punish illegal and criminal acts and firmly safeguard the legitimate and lawful rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, according to the spokesperson. The comments came after CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis recently stated that the United States is engaging in a broader range of espionage against China including Chinese enterprises, claiming that Chinese firms in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and biotechnology are legitimate targets of such activities. The U.S. moves to overstretch the concept of national security, blur the boundaries between competition and security, and even frame economic competition as a so-called "threat" are essentially driven by the zero-sum, Cold War mentality, the spokesperson said. "U.S. intelligence agencies' acts to interfere with normal economic competition severely damage the expectations of businesses worldwide and sabotage the global market environment for fair competition," the spokesperson stated. While the U.S. side has long accused its trading partners of harming its interests through intelligence theft, U.S. intelligence agencies have engaged in large-scale cyber espionage and intelligence theft around the world. Now, they flagrantly violate international trade rules and intellectual property protection norms by targeting economic competitors through espionage activities, the spokesperson noted, criticizing the U.S. side for applying double standards. Refuting U.S. claims that China poses military and economic threats as "a bandit's rhetoric that inverts black and white" and "malicious slander," the spokesperson called the U.S. acts as suppression and smearing against China. "China's technological breakthroughs in fields such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and biotechnology are the fruits of the dedicated efforts of Chinese researchers and enterprises, by no means prey to be arbitrarily coveted by U.S. intelligence agencies," the spokesperson said. Noting U.S. anxiety over China's technological progress, the spokesperson stated that espionage and hegemonic suppression cannot halt the innovative strides of Chinese enterprises, nor can they win genuine technological leadership. ■

item.title: Multinationals bank on new opportunities as China upgrades services sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
* The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, running from Sept. 9 to 13, has attracted a heavier presence of multinational companies compared to last year, with 473 of these being either Fortune Global 500 firms or industry leaders. * China has actively promoted trade in services and opened its services sector wider. These efforts are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world. * By bringing together governments, international organizations and investors, the fair provides a unique opportunity for exchange, sharing of experiences, and the creation of opportunities. BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Opportunities, partnerships and shared prosperity are among the most frequently mentioned terms by exhibitors and guest speakers who are in Beijing for a major services trade fair. This was evident when Ragnhild Sjoner Syrstad, Norway's state secretary for industry and commerce, briefed a large crowd at the Norwegian Pavilion on her nation's exhibition at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS). As the guest country of honor for this year's event, Norway has brought firms spanning health, nutrition, design and lifestyle to its pavilion. According to Syrstad, the stronger presence and diversity of Norwegian firms demonstrate the importance Norway places on both the CIFTIS and the business relationship between the two countries. Another example was Alexander Poulev, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister and minister of economy, investment and industry, who explained why his delegation has traveled more than 7,000 km to attend the CIFTIS. He praised the fair as an opportunity to turn the longstanding friendship between Bulgaria and China into concrete investments, stronger trade, and long-term economic cooperation. With the theme of "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features the debut of over 100 new products and services, covering fields such as information and communications, fintech, and digital and intelligent healthcare. A series of forums and business matchmaking activities are also being held. EXPLORE OPPORTUNITIES The 2026 CIFTIS, running from Sept. 9 to 13, has attracted a heavier presence of multinational companies compared to last year, with 473 of these being either Fortune Global 500 firms or industry leaders. During the fair, U.S. pharmaceutical giant Lilly, a Fortune Global 500 company, is showcasing innovative treatment solutions across the fields of metabolic diseases, neuroscience, oncology and immunology. Wang Li, head of Lilly China's drug development and medical affairs center, said that as China's clinical research capabilities and innovation ecosystem have continued to advance, the country has become an indispensable partner in Lilly's global R&D system. In 2024, Lilly established a medical innovation center in Beijing, focusing on enhancing clinical development efficiency, accelerating new drug R&D and implementing medical solutions. In 2025, the firm launched its first overseas innovation incubator, Lilly Gateway Labs, also located in Beijing. Wang said the Lilly innovation incubator not only brings Lilly's expertise in science, management and resource support to local startups but also deeply integrates into Beijing's pharmaceutical industry ecosystem. Banking on China's huge medical market demand, the company announced earlier this year that it planned to invest 3 billion U.S. dollars in China over the coming decade to expand supply-chain production capacity. This decision marked another significant move by the company to deepen its roots in China and support the development of the local healthcare industry. "We will use the CIFTIS as a bridge to actively introduce global innovation into China, and collaborate with top local academic and industrial forces to bring more innovative treatment options to patients, jointly promoting the high-quality development of China's pharmaceutical and health industry," Wang noted. ABB, a global leader in electrification and automation technologies and also a Fortune Global 500 company, is eyeing the vast business potential arising from China's urban renewal. Lars Eckerlein, general manager of ABB China Limited, said China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) opens a new chapter for the nation's real estate and construction sectors. He added that the company is proud to leverage its expertise in construction and renovation to support China's urban renewal and its sustainability and high-quality development goals. Speaking about his firm's participation in projects across China, from renovating aging buildings to improving energy efficiency, Eckerlein said the Shekou Tower renovation in Shenzhen in south China had achieved an energy-saving rate of 75 percent and cut carbon emissions by 142 tonnes annually. The project also helped remove potential hazards posed by outdated facilities, using an integrated energy management solution. Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said China has actively promoted trade in services and opened its services sector wider. These efforts are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world, he said in a keynote speech delivered at the 2026 Global Trade in Services Summit that marked the opening of the fair. China runs a deficit in services trade, with its imports growing steadily. The value of annual services imports has stood at around 4.4 trillion yuan (about 650 billion U.S. dollars) per year in recent years. BUILD PARTNERSHIPS As the first national-level comprehensive services trade exhibition in the opening year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan, the CIFTIS not only injects fresh vitality into global services trade, investment and consumption, but also serves as a platform for promoting openness and cooperation among countries and fostering mutually beneficial partnerships. Poulev, the Bulgarian deputy prime minister, said trade in services is an important pillar of bilateral ties. "We want to see more organic products reaching the Chinese market and more Bulgarian companies building long-term partnerships with Chinese businesses." He also said that Chinese companies have globally competitive technologies in sectors like electric mobility, software, automation, robotics and advanced manufacturing, while Bulgaria has skilled engineers and an established industrial ecosystem. "This creates a strong opportunity that combines Chinese technology and investment with Bulgarian engineering and expertise," he said, adding that Bulgaria also offers a strategic location for companies looking to expand their presence in Europe. In Poulev's view, stronger investment cooperation can create new supply chains and enhance the value of bilateral trade. "We are ready to build the next generation of Bulgaria-China economic cooperation together." This willingness to build stronger partnerships resonates with the African region. In a video address to the summit, Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye, who also serves as the current chairperson of the African Union, said that the CIFTIS, as one of the world's largest platforms for trade in services, embodies a vision of openness, cooperation and shared development. By bringing together governments, international organizations and investors, this fair provides a unique opportunity for exchange, sharing of experiences, and the creation of opportunities, he said. "In a constantly changing world, we need more than ever to move forward together, share our experiences, and innovate to create new opportunities and build a better future for our countries," he said, adding that efforts should be doubled to turn trade in services into a true driver of shared prosperity, sustainable growth and economic development. PROMOTE PROSPERITY Ding, the Chinese vice premier, pointed out that trade in services is an important component of international trade and is playing an increasingly important role in driving global economic growth and industrial upgrading. He said that amid the accelerating restructuring of the international economic and trade landscape, advancing trade in services and promoting opening up and cooperation in the services sector is not only China's choice but also a necessity for the world. Johanna Hill, deputy director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO), told the summit in a video address that services account for around half of global trade in value-added terms. This share is only likely to grow, propelled by the rise of digital technologies, notably AI. At the same time, services are becoming an ever more important part of global supply chains. They support not only production, but also design, management, logistics and distribution. Against the background of complex and sometimes frail international trade relations, she said countries that have successfully integrated services trade in their development strategies can share their experience and support those that are still making the transition. Hill also said that China is already helping translate its experience into practical support via cooperation with the WTO. The South-South capacity building program, additionally, provides an important vehicle for doing this, by supporting developing countries in areas such as services trade, investment facilitation and electronic commerce. According to Standard Chartered's Benjamin Hung, the next phase of trade will increasingly be shaped by the flow of services, in particular, in the form of knowledge, standards and ideas. "Through years of reform and opening up, China has become one of the world's leading trading nations and a major contributor to global growth and prosperity," Hung said, adding that Standard Chartered has been privileged to both witness this journey firsthand and take part in it. "We live in a world of increasing fragmentation, yet trade remains one of the few truly universal languages, connecting people, markets and opportunities across borders. Trade works best when it is open, transparent, predictable and rules-based," he said. (Video reporters: Wang Xiunan and Xia Zilin; Video editors: Liu Yutian, Roger Lott, Zhang Mocheng, Liu Xiaorui, and Cao Ying)■

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting to make further arrangements on ensuring workplace safety. Workplace safety accidents have occurred frequently in recent times, with profound lessons to be learned, the meeting said. It urged an in-depth investigation into the causes of these accidents and strong measures to address the problems identified. Efforts should be made to further tighten workplace safety responsibilities and address risks and potential hazards in key industries and areas, it said. Any violations of laws and regulations must be dealt with resolutely to firmly uphold the bottom line of workplace safety, effectively curb major accidents, and safeguard people's lives and property, according to the meeting. The meeting also reviewed progress on developing computing networks and upgrading aging reservoirs. Computing networks provide the fundamental support for the development of artificial intelligence, the meeting said, calling for efforts to improve computing infrastructure and actively advance the research, development and application of key technologies and equipment. Coordinated development of computing capacity and electricity supply, as well as the integration of computing and communications networks, should be promoted, said the meeting. The role of market mechanisms should be better leveraged to support enterprises in technological innovation and application as well as resource integration, it added. The meeting stressed the need to comprehensively improve the safety of aging reservoirs and make their renovation and upgrading more targeted and effective. Noting the achievements over the past year in elevating China to a leading country in education, the meeting called for the appropriate allocation of educational resources in response to changes in the school-age population to better meet the needs arising from enrollment peaks at different stages of education. To meet national strategic needs, efforts should focus on cultivating outstanding innovative talent, continuously optimizing the structure of academic disciplines and majors, strengthening the development of textbook systems, and improving talent training models, according to the meeting. The meeting also advocated for a health-first approach to education, aiming to promote students' physical and mental well-being as well as their all-round development. The meeting also reviewed and approved a draft revision to the Regulation on the Administration of Foundations. Greater efforts should be made to strengthen the credibility of foundations, further standardize their management and improve relevant systems, so as to promote the sound and orderly development of China's public interest activities and charities, it said. ■

item.title: From Bishkek to New Delhi, Xi advocates Global South cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is heading to New Delhi for this year's BRICS gathering just over a week after he took part in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. The two back-to-back multilateral engagements converge on a single, defining theme: galvanizing solidarity and cooperation across the Global South. EXPANDING FAMILY The SCO "takes root in the Global South, its heart beats with the Global South, and it is an important pillar of South-South cooperation," Xi said at the Bishkek summit concluded on Tuesday last week, calling on the SCO to "promote the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom." The Chinese leader is expected to put forward further proposals on Global South cooperation at the upcoming BRICS summit, as he has noted that the BRICS is "standing at the forefront of the Global South." This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO and the 20th anniversary of the BRICS cooperation mechanism, both milestone occasions. Riding the wave of the collective rise of the Global South, BRICS and the SCO have over the years expanded their membership and broadened their networks of developing partners. Their members jointly account for more than half of the world's population and about 30 percent of the global economy. This illustrates the fact that the two groupings have evolved into major platforms for Global South cooperation. Xi has not only joined other leaders of member countries in pushing for their respective expansions, but also put forward new ideas and initiatives like the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach and the building of an SCO community with a shared future, opening up new vistas for win-win cooperation among Global South countries. "China has consistently provided a clear vision and momentum for BRICS and the SCO, both conceptually and practically," said Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia. "It transformed BRICS from a relatively exclusive grouping into a broader platform for cooperation among developing countries and the wider Global South," he added. DEVELOPMENT FIRST At the SCO summit last week, Xi called on countries to "stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity." Amid a turbulent and rapidly changing international landscape, development still faces severe challenges, and the road to prosperity for the Global South will not be straight. "The Global South emerges for development and prospers through development. We should make ourselves the main driving force for common development," Xi said during the 2024 BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia. For Xi, development has always been a priority. He sees it as "the master key to solving all problems," and has consistently called for countries worldwide to jointly pursue development and prosperity. Xi has stressed repeatedly that no one should be left behind in the fight against poverty in China, and has led a formidable campaign that ended extreme poverty nationwide, which was hailed as "the greatest anti-poverty achievement in history." His "leaving-no-one-behind" conviction also extends to his efforts to support poverty reduction and spur development across the Global South. "On the path to modernization, no one, and no country, should be left behind," Xi said. Last week in Bishkek, Xi called for consolidating cooperation in both traditional and emerging fields, from trade, investment, connectivity and energy to artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and green industries. Responding to the Global South's aspirations for common development and modernization, Xi has proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI), which marks its fifth anniversary this year. In the last five years, the GDI has mobilized more than 23 billion U.S. dollars, provided support for over 1,800 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, and sponsored training programs for more than 200,000 people in different professions. Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper, said: "Under Xi's leadership, the concept of development has acquired a new international dimension and become part of a broader vision for humanity's shared future." GREATER VOICE As the Global South rises, it deserves a bigger say in global affairs. Last year's SCO Tianjin summit witnessed Xi's proposal of the Global Governance Initiative, a major proposition of China to advance a more just and equitable global governance system. At the heart of this vision is the conviction that every country has a place and an equal role to play in global governance. Xi has long argued that international affairs should not be dictated by those with more muscles. "World affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all," he said in Bishkek last week. "The domination of international affairs by a few is an injustice left over from history, and global governance dictated by one, a few or a bloc of countries is not true multilateralism." "As an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs," Xi said. Over the years, the SCO and BRICS have grown into vital venues for Global South countries to articulate their interests, coordinate their positions and strengthen their collective influence. Their growing role can be seen in political coordination. The two groupings have issued statements on international and regional hotspot issues. In March this year, for example, SCO member states issued a statement expressing grave concern over developments in the Middle East and the strikes on Iran. Xi has also pushed for improving global economic and financial governance. In 2014, Xi and other BRICS leaders formally signed an agreement establishing the New Development Bank, creating a new channel for financing infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging markets and developing countries. At the SCO Bishkek summit, the members reaffirmed the importance of establishing the SCO Development Bank. Now the push for a greater say is extending into emerging areas that will shape the future. In July this year, Xi announced the creation of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, and called for joint efforts to build a just and equitable system of global AI governance. "We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides, promote sustainable development, and prevent creating new historical injustice in AI," Xi said. Beyond the SCO and BRICS, China has also promoted cooperation and greater representation for the Global South through frameworks such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation and the China-ASEAN summit. Xi has said on many occasions that China has always been a member of the Global South and will always belong to the developing world. "No matter how the international landscape evolves, we in China will always keep the Global South in our heart, and maintain our roots in the Global South," he once said.■
